Executive Director of Finance

Detailed Job Description

Position Overview

The Executive Director of Finance is responsible for providing strategic leadership and comprehensive oversight of the company’s financial management functions, including financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, cash flow management, financial analysis, and internal financial controls. This role ensures that the company’s financial operations are aligned with its overall strategic objectives, while supporting organizational growth, profitability enhancement, and long-term financial stability.

The Executive Director of Finance works closely with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Chief Executive Officer (CEO), senior management team, department heads, and business unit managers to develop financial strategies, evaluate business performance, manage financial resources, and provide support for key management decisions. This position plays a critical role in strengthening financial governance, improving the efficiency of financial management, and ensuring the accuracy and transparency of the company’s financial operations.

Key Responsibilities

I. Financial Strategy and Senior Leadership

Develop and implement financial strategies that align with the company’s business objectives, operational priorities, and long-term development plans. Provide financial guidance to senior management regarding investment decisions, resource allocation, cost management, and business expansion opportunities. Establish financial policies, management standards, and performance targets to strengthen financial discipline and ensure that all financial activities remain consistent with the company’s overall strategy.

II. Financial Planning, Budgeting, and Forecasting

Take full responsibility for the preparation and execution of annual budgets, periodic financial forecasts, and long-term financial plans. Coordinate with department heads and business unit leaders to set financial targets, assess capital requirements, and allocate financial resources effectively. Continuously monitor budget execution, analyze financial variances, and propose corrective or improvement measures to maintain cost efficiency and achieve established financial goals.

III. Financial Reporting and Performance Analysis

Oversee the preparation, review, and submission of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports. Ensure that financial statements, management reports, and performance analysis data are accurate, timely, and compliant with applicable accounting standards. Evaluate the company’s revenue performance, operating expenses, profitability, cash flow, and financial trends to provide actionable insights that support senior management decision-making and the improvement of business performance.

IV. Cash Flow and Financial Resource Management

Supervise cash flow planning, working capital management, liquidity monitoring, and the allocation of financial resources. Establish relevant management procedures to ensure the company maintains sufficient cash reserves, fulfills its financial obligations, and meets the requirements of daily business operations. Collaborate with treasury, accounting, and banking partners to optimize cash management practices, monitor capital requirements, and strengthen the company’s overall financial position.

V. Financial Risk Management and Internal Control

Establish and maintain a robust system of financial controls, risk management procedures, and corporate financial governance standards. Identify and assess potential financial risks related to expenditures, investments, credit, liquidity, and operational activities. Work with internal audit, compliance, legal, and accounting teams to strengthen internal controls, address anomalies in financial management, and ensure that financial processes adhere to company policies and relevant regulatory requirements.

VI. Investment Evaluation and Strategic Financial Support

Conduct financial evaluations of business expansion plans, capital investment proposals, strategic projects, and potential mergers and acquisitions. Develop financial models to analyze return on investment (ROI), assess the financial feasibility of projects, and provide professional recommendations to senior management. Collaborate with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and the senior leadership team to support capital allocation decisions, financial restructuring initiatives, and other strategic corporate development activities.

VII. Financial Compliance and Coordination with External Stakeholders

Ensure that the company’s financial management activities comply with applicable accounting standards, tax requirements, regulatory obligations, and corporate governance policies. Coordinate with external auditors, tax advisors, financial institutions, and other professional service providers as necessary. Oversee the preparation of financial documentation, audit materials, and compliance reports to ensure transparency and accountability in financial operations.

VIII. Financial Leadership and Process Improvement

Lead and develop the company’s finance team, encompassing functions such as financial planning, accounting, financial reporting, and financial analysis. Define departmental objectives, performance standards, staff development plans, and operational accountability mechanisms. Evaluate financial management systems, reporting technologies, and business processes to enhance operational efficiency, improve the accuracy of financial data, and drive continuous improvement within the finance function.

Qualifications

Education

A bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, business administration, or a related field is required. A master’s degree in finance, accounting, or business administration (MBA) is preferred. Preference will be given to candidates who hold professional qualifications such as Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA), or Certified Management Accountant (CMA).

Work Experience

Typically, candidates should possess 15 to 18 or more years of progressively responsible experience in finance, accounting, financial planning, or corporate financial management, including at least 5 years in a senior financial management or executive leadership role.

Candidates must have extensive experience in overseeing financial planning and analysis (FP&A), budgeting, financial forecasting, financial reporting, cash flow management, internal controls, and financial risk assessment. They should demonstrate the ability to lead finance teams, manage complex financial operations, develop financial strategies, and provide expert decision-making advice to senior management. Preference will be given to those with experience in supporting business expansion, capital investment decisions, organizational restructuring, or financial management across multiple business units.

Furthermore, the SRVP is responsible for cultivating regional management talent, optimizing operational systems, and enhancing market competitiveness to ensure long-term, stable business growth and operational success within the assigned region.

Key Responsibilities

I. Regional Strategic Planning and Leadership

Develop and implement long-term development strategies and annual operational plans for the assigned region, ensuring that regional objectives are aligned with the company’s overall strategy, financial goals, and market development direction. Analyze the regional market environment, industry trends, competitive landscape, and customer needs to identify new business opportunities and potential risks. Establish regional management standards and execution mechanisms, define the responsibilities, objectives, and performance requirements for each business unit, and drive the effective implementation of regional strategies.

Coordinate activities across different departments within the region to resolve significant issues that impact business execution and operational efficiency.

III. Financial Management and Operational Goal Control

Oversee regional budget development, financial planning, cost control, and the analysis of operational results, ensuring that regional financial objectives align with the company’s overall financial plan. Collaborate with the CFO and the finance team to review regional revenue, profit, operating expenses, cash flow, and return on investment (ROI). Establish mechanisms for monitoring budget execution and financial performance; control operating costs effectively; enhance the efficiency of regional resource utilization; and ensure that all business units achieve their established financial objectives.

IV. Market Expansion and Business Growth

Lead regional market development, business expansion, and commercial growth initiatives, identifying potential customer segments, emerging markets, and strategic partnership opportunities. Oversee the development of sales channels, customer acquisition, marketing campaigns, and business collaborations to drive the growth of regional market share and enhance corporate brand influence. Partner with business development, sales, and marketing teams to formulate market-entry strategies and customer growth plans, ensuring the sustained competitiveness of the regional business.

Responsible for establishing and refining the regional management structure, and overseeing the performance of regional department heads and senior management. Define team performance objectives, talent development programs, and succession plans for management roles to strengthen regional organizational capabilities and the execution proficiency of the leadership team. Oversee the management of key regional customer relationships, strategic partnerships, and major commercial contracts, ensuring timely responses to customer needs and the stability of collaborative ties. Collaborate with customer success, sales, and operations teams to improve customer satisfaction, retention rates, and long-term partnership value.

Monitor operational, financial, legal, and market risks within regional business activities, and establish effective mechanisms for risk identification, assessment, and mitigation. Ensure that all regional business units comply with applicable laws, industry regulations, internal corporate policies, and regulatory requirements. Work with legal, compliance, finance, and internal audit teams to periodically review regional management processes and internal controls, addressing significant compliance issues promptly and driving the implementation of corrective actions.

VIII. Communication with Senior Management and Strategic Execution

Provide regular reports to the CEO, COO, and the corporate executive management team regarding regional operational performance, market developments, financial results, business risks, and the progress of strategic plan execution. Provide management counsel regarding regional expansion, organizational restructuring, major investments, and business transformation. Facilitate the sharing of resources and information between various regions and corporate headquarters, ensure the unified execution of corporate strategy at the regional level, and drive long-term, sustainable growth for regional operations.

jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. RSM is seeking a growth-oriented Management Consulting Director to join our Technology Performance practice. This leader will play a critical role in driving the continued growth of the practice by expanding strategic client relationships, developing new market opportunities, and leading complex technology transformation engagements.

This Director will combine strong business development capabilities with deep expertise in Technology Strategy, ERP Strategy, IT Architecture, and complex transformation program leadership. The role requires a leader who can originate opportunities, shape solutions, build trusted executive relationships, oversee complex engagements, and develop high-performing consulting teams.

The ideal candidate is a proven consulting leader who can connect business strategy with technology, helping organizations make critical technology investment decisions, modernize their enterprise environments, and successfully execute large-scale transformation initiatives. This individual will also help shape the continued evolution of the Technology Performance practice by developing talent, strengthening capabilities, and bringing differentiated solutions to market.

Responsibilities

Practice Growth & Market Leadership

Drive growth of the Technology Performance practice through business development, account expansion, relationship building, and new client acquisition.
Build and manage a strong pipeline of technology consulting and transformation opportunities.
Develop trusted relationships with senior executives, including CIOs, CTOs, CFOs, COOs, and other business and technology leaders.
Lead strategic pursuits from opportunity identification and solution development through proposal creation, executive presentations, and contract award.
Identify opportunities to expand existing client relationships by connecting business priorities with RSM’s broader technology and consulting capabilities.
Develop and execute go-to-market strategies around key Technology Performance offerings and emerging client needs.
Contribute to the practice’s market presence through thought leadership, industry events, executive presentations, and development of differentiated offerings.

Client & Engagement Leadership

Serve as a senior trusted advisor to executives navigating complex technology strategies, investments, and transformation programs.
Lead engagements spanning Technology Strategy, ERP Strategy and Selection, IT Architecture, enterprise application modernization, digital transformation, and technology operating model design.
Advise clients on aligning technology investments and roadmaps with business strategy, growth objectives, operational needs, and financial priorities.
Lead and oversee complex, multi-workstream transformation programs involving business stakeholders, technology teams, vendors, and third-party partners.
Lead executive workshops, technology assessments, and strategy sessions and translate findings into actionable transformation roadmaps.
Provide executive oversight across engagements, ensuring high-quality delivery, strong client relationships, financial performance, appropriate risk management, and successful business outcomes.
Support clients through significant business and technology events, including enterprise modernization, organizational growth, transactions, integrations, carve-outs, and large-scale transformation initiatives.

Technology Transformation Leadership

Serve as a subject matter expert in technology strategy and transformation, bringing a strong point of view on how organizations can use technology to enable business growth and improve performance.
Lead technology strategy and roadmap development, including assessment of current-state capabilities, identification of gaps, investment prioritization, and future-state planning.
Advise clients on ERP strategy, modernization, selection, implementation planning, and optimization, including the broader business and operating model implications of ERP transformation.
Assess existing IT and enterprise architecture and develop future-state architectures that support scalability, integration, modernization, and business objectives.
Provide leadership across complex technology environments involving ERP, cloud, data and analytics, AI, automation, enterprise applications, infrastructure, and integration architecture.
Bring structure, governance, and executive leadership to large and complex transformation programs, including program strategy, executive governance, vendor coordination, risk management, dependency management, and stakeholder alignment.
Evaluate technology environments and recommend practical, business-focused solutions that balance modernization goals, investment requirements, organizational readiness, and risk.
Stay current on emerging technologies, market trends, ERP platforms, AI capabilities, and evolving technology operating models and translate those developments into practical client solutions and new market opportunities.

People & Practice Leadership

Lead, mentor, and develop consulting professionals across multiple levels, creating a culture of high performance, accountability, collaboration, and continuous development.
Build scalable consulting capabilities by developing talent, methodologies, intellectual capital, and repeatable solutions.
Coach and develop team members while identifying and preparing future leaders within the practice.
Collaborate with practice leadership on recruiting, workforce planning, capability development, and strategic investments needed to support continued growth.
Foster collaboration across RSM service lines and capabilities to deliver integrated solutions and create broader client relationships.
Help establish and maintain standards for engagement quality, client service, delivery excellence, and team performance.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor’s degree.
12+ years of management consulting, technology consulting, or technology transformation experience, including progressively increasing leadership responsibility.
Demonstrated experience selling, shaping, and delivering complex technology consulting engagements.
Proven track record of business development, account growth, executive relationship management, and consulting sales.
Deep experience in one or more core areas including Technology Strategy, ERP Strategy, IT Architecture, or large-scale technology transformation.
Experience leading complex, multi-workstream programs involving business stakeholders, technology teams, vendors, and executive leadership.
Strong understanding of enterprise technology environments, including ERP platforms, enterprise applications, cloud, data and analytics, integration, AI, and automation.
Demonstrated ability to translate business strategy and operational requirements into technology roadmaps, architectures, and investment priorities.
Strong project and program management capabilities, with experience leading complex initiatives across multiple stakeholders, workstreams, technologies, and vendors.
Experience leading and developing multidisciplinary consulting teams.
Strong executive presence with the ability to advise and influence C-suite and senior business and technology leaders.
Exceptional communication, presentation, facilitation, and relationship-building skills.
Strong commercial and financial acumen, including experience managing engagement economics, delivery quality, risk, and client expectations.
Ability and willingness to travel based on client and business needs, up to 50% (Canada and US)

Preferred

Experience advising clients within Private Equity, Real Estate, Construction, Consumer Products/CPG, or other complex business environments.
Experience supporting technology strategy and transformation across the Private Equity transaction lifecycle, including technology due diligence, post-close planning, integrations, carve-outs, and portfolio company transformation.
Experience working with construction, real estate, or capital-intensive organizations with complex technology, ERP, project management, or operational environments.
Experience leading ERP modernization, enterprise application transformation, or ERP strategy and selection initiatives.
Experience developing enterprise, solution, or technology architecture strategies within complex IT environments.
Experience overseeing major transformation programs involving multiple workstreams, vendors, platforms, and executive stakeholders.
Experience developing go-to-market strategies, building consulting offerings, and helping scale a technology consulting practice.
Relevant advanced degree or professional certifications in areas such as enterprise architecture, ERP, cloud, program management, or technology transformation.

jobs.description:
Please note the base salary for this role is $225,000.00 CAD.

The Head of Credit & Portfolio Management is the senior leader of the Portfolio Management (PM) function across Global Corporate Banking in Canada and the U.S. The role owns PM governance, standards and risk oversight. It serves as the senior PM approval authority within the delegated lending framework, leads active portfolio management and credit structuring excellence, and is the principal Corporate Banking representative to Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and regulators on PM matters.

The role sets the standards and the operating model. Lending Unit PM leaders own business execution, staffing and portfolio outcomes. The role partners with Risk & Financial Management, Capital Markets and Global Transaction Banking, and applies effective challenge within BMO’s Risk Appetite framework.

Key Accountabilities

Governance & Standards
Act as the key governance driver for the PM function; own PM standards, policy interpretation and governance consistency across Corporate Banking.
Maintain a common PM operating playbook across LUs, standardizing intent and repeatable work rather than org models.
Provide Corporate Banking input to BMO corporate policies and lending directives, and ensure policies are interpreted and applied correctly.
Hold a standing seat on credit and risk committees as a delegate to the Co-Heads of Global Corporate Banking, with a documented escalation protocol.
Credit Governance & Approval Authority
Exercise delegated approval authority within delegated limits for transactions above LU PM head authority.
Serve as delegate for Business Head signoffs for the Co-Heads of Global Corporate Banking.
Provide effective challenge on material credit, underwriting and portfolio risk; escalate significant policy, governance or risk concerns.
Represent Corporate Banking on the U.S. Allowance Committee and contribute to the allowance and provisioning outlook.
Ensure risk-taking stays within the Risk Appetite framework, agreed limits and regulatory requirements.
Regulatory, Audit & Control Leadership
Act as the primary PM representative with Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and regulators; lead on exams and reviews relating to Corporate Banking.
Lead PM-related remediation and regulatory change initiatives; act as direct counterpart to 2nd and 3rd line workstreams.
Ensure control effectiveness and audit readiness, including 1st line quality assurance of credit processes.
Portfolio Monitoring & Risk Insights
Act as chief architect of the KRI dashboard and wider monitoring controls; own a common Corporate Banking PM reporting framework covering KRIs, watchlist migration, EWIs and past dues.
Provide management insight on portfolio trends, concentrations and emerging risks, including sector and macro developments, working with sector heads and Industry Verticals.
Direct oversight of high-risk accounts: risk-rating accuracy, timely action on deteriorating credits, and Special Assets liaison with lessons-learned sessions.
Contribute stress testing and scenario analysis inputs for the Corporate Banking portfolio.
Own the PM data and reporting technology roadmap to establish a common fact base.
Active Portfolio Management & Capital Productivity
Maintain a Corporate Banking de-risking playbook with trigger frameworks for emerging risk and shifting concentrations.
Provide Corporate Banking input to the industry, single-name, tenor and product limit framework, and monitor the portfolio against it.
Partner with Capital Markets on hold levels, distribution, hedging and risk-transfer levers.
Maintain a long-term portfolio view that balances profitable growth with credit quality.
Credit Products & Structuring
Define the new-deal hand-off from origination to PM, clarifying deal understanding, owners and post-close items.
Support LUs that elect a greater PM role in new-business underwriting; origination retains client ownership and negotiation.
Provide structuring expertise and coaching on complex transactions; evaluate new and tailored financing structures and related policy changes.
Talent & Capability Development
Establish PM competency standards, training curriculum and career frameworks, coordinating with the Training working group.
Lead PM succession planning and talent development; set junior staffing principles that allow flexible deployment across LUs.
PM Effectiveness & Operating Model
Drive process simplification, automation and operating-model enhancements across PM workflows.
Oversee centralized mid-to-back-office support (LC, TPS, KYC), with PM retaining risk decisions and accountability.
Oversee PM KPIs and performance measurements across Corporate Banking, in coordination with the KPI task force.
Continue oversight and management of the BA team.
Leadership & Culture
Promote the Bank’s risk culture: clear accountabilities, open communication, effective challenge and tone from the top.
Lead and mentor a diverse team; develop leaders, plan succession and attract and retain top talent.
Foster an inclusive environment and a high-performance culture; role model One Bank leadership and the Bank’s Ambition.

Qualifications

Post-secondary education or equivalent work experience; CPA or MBA or equivalent experience in finance, accounting and business law.
20+ years in financial services in a corporate lending environment developing business; 10+ years negotiating and structuring financial transactions with expertise in Leveraged Finance.
Credit qualified, with expert knowledge of credit risk management and credit philosophy, policies and procedures.
Working knowledge of U.S. and/or Canadian regulatory expectations; experience leading regulator and Internal Audit engagements.
Command of portfolio management concepts: allowance and provisioning, RWA, return on capital, concentration and limit frameworks.
Expertise across key corporate lending sectors, with in-depth knowledge of corporate banking products and services.
Experience managing a large, diverse team and influencing LU leaders where decision rights are shared.
Highly developed written and oral communication and relationship-building skills.
Expert analytical thinking, change leadership, negotiation and risk management; in-depth strategic business planning.

The Clarice Overview

The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center (The Clarice) at the University of Maryland (UMD) is part of the College of Arts and Humanities (ARHU) and is the academic and artistic home of the School of Music (SOM); the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS); the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library (MSPAL); and The Clarice’s own artistic platform Clarice Presents (CP). At the time of its construction, the 318,000-square-foot facility on 17 acres of land was the largest construction project undertaken by the State of Maryland, and remains one of the most complex projects in recent Maryland state history.

The Clarice opened in 2001 and is named in honor of visual artist and philanthropist Clarice Smith (1933-2021). From its founding, The Clarice was conceived as a “creative village” that brought a robust series of outside artists and performers to campus, supported the academic and performance programs of SOM and TDPS and collaborations with MSPAL, and built bridges between UMD and its surrounding community. The Clarice, through its dynamic outreach programs, manifested UMD’s commitment to meaningfully contribute to those communities through the arts and the encouragement of cultural citizenship. The Clarice continues to strengthen its role as the central home for performing arts at UMD, supporting the academic and performance needs of SOM and TDPS, ensuring the excellence and social relevance of all of its programs, and enhancing its leadership position in the field despite the political and financial headwinds for the arts in this country.

The Clarice hosts more than 1,000 public performances and events each year, the majority featuring the artistry of SOM and TDPS students and faculty. The Clarice’s artistic platform, Clarice Presents (CP), offers uniquely integrated performances, digital, civic and community engagement programming. MSPAL, often in partnership with CP and M‐NCPPC, also presents events at The Clarice. All presentations and events are supported by the administrative, production management, and technical staff of The Clarice.

In collaboration with the Directors of the resident academic units, the position is responsible for the Clarice’s artistic programming and works to ensure that this programming and other initiatives respond to curricular needs. The Executive Director works alongside Directors of the School of Music; the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies; and the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library, as well as the Executive Director of Arts for All to develop and refine a strategic and innovative vision that enhances the curricular experience for faculty and students, engages the campus, connects with the community, and further enhances the reputation of the University of Maryland. The Executive Director should bring significant knowledge of the changing performing arts landscape and a fierce dedication to collaborative leadership models. The Executive Director meets monthly with the Dean and annually with the Provost and Dean to ensure that the performing arts have a campus and community-wide agenda and impact. For more detailed information about The Clarice please visit this website.

We are looking for our next AVP, Direct Channel Lead, to help shape and execute Aviva Canada’s Direct distribution strategy and drive profitable, sustainable growth across the channel. This role will translate strategy and channel performance insights into clear priorities and targeted actions across portfolio performance, customer outcomes, sales and service, digital, marketing, pricing, underwriting, product, technology and operations.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Personal Insurance, the AVP will lead the cross-functional Direct agenda, strengthen governance and performance management, and advance transformation and continuous improvement initiatives that improve growth, profitability, efficiency and customer experience.

Come join our team!

What You'll Do

Support the development and execution of Aviva Canada’s Direct distribution strategy, business plan and multi-year roadmap, with clear priorities for profitable growth, portfolio performance, customer outcomes and competitive differentiation.
Lead the cross-functional Direct agenda, partnering across Sales & Service, Digital, Marketing, Product, Pricing, Underwriting, Claims, Technology, Finance and Performance Management to align priorities and accelerate delivery.
Translate financial, customer, sales, service, underwriting, operational and portfolio data into clear insights, targeted business actions and recommendations for senior leaders.
Establish and maintain effective channel governance, performance measures, decision forums and reporting to ensure clear accountability for strategic initiatives, financial outcomes and operational execution.
Drive portfolio performance and clean-up actions across Direct and relevant Affinity businesses, identifying leakage and opportunities to improve growth, profitability, retention and customer outcomes.
Advance the Direct transformation and continuous improvement agenda, maintaining a prioritized backlog of technology and non-technology initiatives that support growth, profitability, efficiency, and customer experience.
Provide respectful challenge and remove barriers across the cross-functional team to improve productivity, execution, and delivery.
Lead competitor and market intelligence for the Direct channel, including pricing developments, digital capabilities, customer experience innovation, emerging technology and evolving customer needs.
Support the development and evolution of Direct and Affinity propositions, ensuring alignment with customer needs, Aviva’s Personal Insurance strategy, and risk appetite.
Keep stakeholders informed of priorities, progress, decisions, risks and roadblocks, escalating issues where required.
Ensure customer interests, fair outcomes, regulatory requirements and risk management expectations are embedded in channel decisions and change initiatives.
Role model Aviva’s values and behaviors, promoting a One Aviva culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, continuous improvement and customer focus.

What You'll Bring

Significant Canadian Personal Insurance experience, ideally including Direct, digital, consumer or multi-channel insurance.
Strong technical and commercial understanding of Personal Insurance portfolio performance, including pricing, underwriting, product, segmentation, loss ratio, rate adequacy, customer acquisition and retention.
Demonstrated experience translating complex channel and portfolio data into strategic priorities, recommendations and targeted business actions.
Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional work with shared accountability across sales, service, digital, marketing, pricing, underwriting, product, technology and operations.
Strong financial and business acumen, with the ability to understand P&L drivers and balance growth, profitability, risk and customer outcomes.
Experience leading transformation, continuous improvement, or strategic initiatives in a dynamic and complex operating environment.
Excellent communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to simplify complex issues and influence senior leaders and partners.
Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to establish trust and credibility with internal and external partners.
A customer-led, strategic and commercially minded approach, with curiosity about market trends, technology and emerging innovation.
Experience with Affinity, partnerships, bancassurance or B2B relationship management is an asset.
CIP, FCIP, or equivalent designation is an asset.

What You'll Get

The salary band for this position ranges from $160000 to $185,000. Please note that individual salary is determined by factors such as job-related knowledge, skills and experience, as well as internal equity.
Hybrid flexible work model.
Outstanding career development opportunities.
We’ll support your professional development education.
Competitive vacation package with the option to purchase 5 extra days off per year.
Employee-driven programs focused on gender, LGBTQ+, origins, diversity, and inclusion.

new_jobs.title: Regional Director Clinic Support
new_jobs.description:
We’re Hiring a Regional Director – Hamilton Area, Anytime Clinics

Previous operational leadership experience within the dental industry is required for this position.

Passion Dental Group is looking for an experienced Regional Director to lead and support our Anytime Clinics across the Hamilton area. We’re seeking a hands-on leader with strong dental operations experience and a proven ability to build teams, develop leaders and improve clinic performance.

You understand that successful clinics depend on effective operations, engaged people and accessible, patient-centred care. You know how to identify what’s working, address what needs improvement and bring teams together around clear priorities. Whether you’re coaching a Clinic Manager, partnering with a Doctor or working through an operational challenge, you bring a practical, collaborative approach that builds trust and delivers results.

The Opportunity

As Regional Director, you’ll oversee the operational performance of our Hamilton-area Anytime Clinics, working closely with Clinic Managers, Doctors and Support Office partners to strengthen teams, improve day-to-day operations and support sustainable growth.

You’ll help each clinic succeed by understanding the people, processes and opportunities behind its results. You’ll provide clear direction, establish accountability and ensure clinic leaders have the support and tools they need to lead effectively.

Within the Anytime Clinics environment, you’ll help teams balance patient access and responsiveness with effective scheduling, staffing and consistent service. Your focus will be on helping clinics meet patient needs while building strong, sustainable operations.

This is a hands-on, clinic-facing role requiring regular in-person visits and travel between clinics throughout the Hamilton area.

What Great Looks Like

You’re an operational leader who knows how to build strong teams. You’re comfortable reviewing financial performance and equally comfortable spending time in a clinic to understand workflow challenges, support a manager or help a team work better together.

In This Role, You Will

Strengthen clinic operations: Improve workflows, scheduling, staffing and resource utilization. Help teams implement practical solutions that support efficient operations and an exceptional patient experience.
Support patient access: Partner with clinic leaders to align appointment availability, team capacity and provider coverage with patient demand. Help teams respond effectively to urgent and evolving scheduling needs.
Build strong, engaged teams: Partner with Clinic Managers and People & Culture to recruit, onboard, develop and retain great people. Encourage collaboration, address team challenges and create an environment where expectations are clear and people feel supported.
Develop accountable leaders: Coach Clinic Managers to take ownership of their clinics, lead confidently and follow through on priorities. Provide meaningful feedback, support performance management and develop future leaders.
Drive business performance: Use KPIs, financial results and operational reporting to identify trends and opportunities. Translate insights into practical improvements across production, collections, treatment acceptance, hygiene utilization, patient retention and profitability.
Deliver on plans and priorities: Support clinics in achieving budgets, annual plans and growth objectives. Establish clear action plans, monitor progress and help leaders overcome barriers.
Build trusted partnerships: Work closely with Doctors and clinical teams to understand clinic needs, support the delivery of patient care and align operational priorities. Connect clinic teams with the right Support Office resources.
Lead change effectively: Guide teams through new programs, processes and operational improvements, ensuring they understand the purpose, expectations and support available.

You know that lasting results come from building capable leaders, effective processes and teams that work well together.

What You Bring

Required: Previous operational leadership experience within the dental industry, including direct responsibility for dental clinic operations, team leadership and business performance.
Strong knowledge of dental clinic workflows and performance drivers, including scheduling, production, collections, treatment acceptance, hygiene utilization and patient retention.
A demonstrated ability to build, develop and retain strong teams, including experience coaching managers and addressing team or performance challenges.
Strong business and financial acumen, with experience using KPIs, budgets and operational reporting to guide decisions and improve results.
A practical approach to problem-solving, with the ability to identify root causes, prioritize competing needs and implement sustainable improvements.
Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with confidence partnering with Doctors, Clinic Managers and Support Office teams.
The ability to balance regional priorities with hands-on support tailored to individual clinics.
Sound judgment and adaptability when responding to changing patient demand, staffing needs and operational priorities.
Availability and flexibility to travel regularly between clinics throughout the Hamilton area.

Five or more years of progressive dental leadership experience and experience overseeing multiple clinics or locations are preferred.

Most importantly, you care about both the people and the performance of your clinics. You set high expectations, provide meaningful support and understand that your success is reflected in the strength of the leaders and teams around you.

About Passion Dental Group

Passion Dental Group is a growing dental organization committed to creating exceptional experiences for both patients and team members. Our clinics and leaders are supported by dedicated teams across Operations, People & Culture, Marketing, Accounting & Finance, Learning and Clinical Development, creating strong partnerships between our clinics and Support Office.

We’re also proud to be Great Place to Work Certified, reflecting our continued commitment to building workplaces where people feel supported, valued and empowered to grow.

Ready to bring your dental operations expertise and passion for building teams to our Hamilton-area Anytime Clinics? Apply today and grow with Passion Dental Group.
